title: Reel Forge
text:
---
name: reel-forge
description: Produce a motion video rendered entirely from code — showreels, product launch films, UI-flow loops, story pieces. Use when someone asks for a launch video, product reel, animated explainer, motion ad, or code-made music video.
---

# Reel Forge

## Ask first
Product and URL · length · formats (9:16, 1:1, 16:9) · brand colours and fonts · a reference (frame, clip, or folder) · music (a file, or "make it").

## Steps
1. **Collect assets.** Visit the URL with a headless browser; save real screens, logo, colours and fonts to `./assets`; list them.
2. **Study the reference**, if there is one → `docs/look.md` (briefs/cards.md, card 3).
3. **Sound plan.** Made music: `node audio/grid.mjs --bpm N --bars M > grid.json`. Supplied track: `python audio/analyze.py track.wav > grid.json`.
4. **Shot list on the grid** → `docs/shots.md`. Show it and wait for approval.
5. **Build the stage.** Copy `engine/reel.html` and `engine/kit.js`; write shots that paint from local time only. Follow `RULES.md`.
6. **Review loop** (card 6) — at least three rounds, until every score is 8+.
7. **Render** `node engine/forge.mjs`, then cues → `node audio/synth.mjs cues.json out/sound.wav`, mux with ffmpeg, export every format.
8. **Deliver** the video, a contact sheet, a poster frame, and a note on what you'd improve next.

## Non-negotiables
- Real product screens only — never invented ones.
- Frames come from time alone: no random, no timers, no CSS transitions while rendering.
- Forbidden looks are listed in `RULES.md`; check every shot against them.

## Checks
```
ffmpeg -i out/reel.mp4 -vf "fps=2,scale=270:-1,tile=6x5" -frames:v 1 out/contact.png    # whole piece at a glance
ffmpeg -ss T -i out/reel.mp4 -vf "scale=320:-1,tile=12x1" -frames:v 1 out/strip.png     # a fast moment, frame by frame
ffmpeg -i out/reel.mp4 -vf "fps=1,scale=360:-1,tile=5x3" -frames:v 1 out/phone.png      # phone-size legibility
ffmpeg -stream_loop 1 -i out/reel.mp4 -c copy out/loop-check.mp4                         # does the loop seam hold?
```
Render the same short range twice with the same settings; the two files must hash identically.

title: SHADDAI Reel Forge
text:
# SHADDAI Reel Forge

Make motion pieces from code — showreels, product films, UI-flow loops, story videos — on demand. TURTLE reaches this through the MCP (`shaddai_turtle_build`, or `gamedev_search` with source `motion-studio`).

## The idea
A model can't output a video file, but it can write a program that knows exactly what the picture looks like at any moment. Reel Forge keeps that program a pure function of time, then lets a headless browser step through time, save each frame, and hand the folder to ffmpeg. Same inputs, same pixels, every time — so any change is a small edit plus a re-render.

## What's inside
| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `RULES.md` | Project rules the agent follows every session |
| `engine/kit.js` | Motion kit: feel-based springs, `chase()` for retargeted values, `stretch()`, `handoff()`, `cycle()`, seeded randomness, beat snapping |
| `engine/reel.html` | The stage: shots paint from local time; built-in motion blur by averaging sub-moments |
| `engine/forge.mjs` | Renderer: local server → numbered frames (resumable) → ffmpeg |
| `audio/grid.mjs` | Beat grid from a tempo (for music you make) |
| `audio/analyze.py` | Beat grid and accents measured from a supplied track |
| `audio/synth.mjs` | Code-made sound effects with six voices and a soft limiter |
| `briefs/cards.md` | Seven briefing cards, quick test to multi-day production |
| `skill/SKILL.md` | The whole pipeline as a reusable skill |

## Quick start
```
npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium     # plus ffmpeg on your PATH
cp -r workflows/reel-forge my-reel && cd my-reel
node engine/forge.mjs --fps 30 --out out/reel.mp4          # renders the starter piece
```
Then paste a card from `briefs/cards.md` to your agent and let it replace the starter shots.

## Ladder
Spark → Product → Look → Flow → Crew. Add Review after every render, Retune when motion feels stiff.

## Quality gate
No piece ships until a Review round scores 8+ on all seven axes and the loop-check seam holds.

## Provenance
This system is SHADDAI's own design, written from first principles; see `NOTICE.md` for the ideas it is informed by and the third-party material kept separately in the library.

title: Provenance notice
text:
# Provenance notice

**Reel Forge code and text are original SHADDAI work.** They were written fresh; no source files, prompts or documentation from other projects were copied.

## General techniques (not owned by anyone)
Deterministic time-driven rendering, damped-spring motion, beat-grid timing, synthesized sound, contact-sheet review loops, and generate-then-trace are common engineering and design practice. The spring formula is standard damped-oscillator mathematics.

## Informed by
Public discussion of code-rendered motion video (September 2026) shaped which problems this system addresses. No text or code from those posts is reproduced here.

## Separate third-party material
The SHADDAI game-dev library (`backend/knowledge/gamedev/`) holds reference material from other open projects, kept under its own source names with licenses recorded in `sources.json`. It must retain its original notices. None of it is part of Reel Forge.

| Source id | License |
|---|---|
| impertio-threejs, mike007jd-superpowers, nicewolf-ecs, opencode-game-studio, agent-sprite-forge | MIT |

As these are replaced by SHADDAI-original equivalents, they are removed from the library.

title: Reel Forge — project rules
text:
# Reel Forge — project rules

Copy this file into the root of any reel project; the agent reads it every session.

## How frames are made
- A reel is a function of time. `__paint(t)` must produce the identical image for the same `t`, always.
- Allowed: arithmetic on `t`, springs from `kit.js`, seeded randomness.
- Not allowed while rendering: CSS transitions, timers, animation callbacks, `Math.random`, anything that remembers the previous frame.
- Output is H.264, `yuv420p`, CRF 15, via `node engine/forge.mjs`.

## Taste
- Rejected by default: a centered title on a gradient; everything fading in together; text or boxes pinned to corners; glowing interface chrome; stock particle bursts.
- One display typeface, one interface typeface, one accent colour unless the brief says otherwise.
- Something new on screen every 2–4 seconds. The first two seconds must hold a viewer by themselves.

## Sound
- Make it in code (`audio/synth.mjs`) unless a track is supplied.
- Hits land on the beat grid (`audio/grid.mjs`, or `analyze.py` for a supplied track). Target about −14 LUFS.

## Before showing anything
1. Render one frame per beat as a contact sheet and look at it.
2. Score it (card 6). Fix the three worst problems. Repeat until every score is 8 or better.
3. Only then render the full piece.

## Effort
Light edits: low effort. New piece: high. A launch film whose first seconds must carry everything: maximum.

## Secrets and sources
Keys live in `.env`, never in prompts or committed files. From any reference, take the grammar (rhythm, scale, type behaviour) — never the content, characters or logos.

title: Briefing cards
text:
# Briefing cards

Seven cards, from a quick test to a multi-day production. Fill the brackets, paste the card to TURTLE (or any agent with a shell), and attach what the card asks for. Start low on the ladder; climb only when the card below is working.

| Card | Use it when | Needs from you |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Spark | testing the pipeline | nothing |
| 2 Product | you have a real product | URL |
| 3 Look | you want a specific style | a reference frame, clip, or folder |
| 4 Flow | you want one element to travel through a story | the list of screens/states |
| 5 Crew | a long, multi-session film | all of the above + budget |
| 6 Review | after any render | the rendered stills |
| 7 Retune | motion feels cheap | the code |

---

## 1 · Spark
```
Make a [SECONDS]-second motion piece that shows off what you can do. Give every shot a
different technique, put the strongest one first, use one accent colour, and build all
graphics from code. Include sound. No text pinned to corners.
```
This card proves the toolchain works. It carries no idea, so don't judge the idea by it.

## 2 · Product
```
Make a [SECONDS]-second film for [PRODUCT] at [URL], vertical first.

Gather: open the site, capture real screens, grab the true logo, colours and fonts into
./assets, and show me the inventory before animating.
Rule: animate the real interface. Never redraw it from memory.

Story, one idea per 2–4 seconds:
  1. The problem, in five words, set huge.
  2. The product assembling itself.
  3. Three capabilities, each a real action performed by a cursor.
  4. One proof number: [NUMBER].
  5. Logo and call to action: [CTA].

Sound: original, [BPM] BPM, made in code, hits on the beat.
Deliver 9:16, then 1:1 and 16:9 from the same timeline, re-laid-out rather than cropped.
Show a one-frame-per-beat contact sheet before the full render.
```
Keep one working session per brand: the renderer and sound tools are then already in place for the next piece.

## 3 · Look
Name a look, or show one. Show the model a frame and say what to take (palette, lettering, grain, rhythm) and what to leave (subject, logos, characters).
```
Reference: ./refs/ (clip, frames, or a folder of my work).

Step 1  Pull a frame every half second. Study them.
Step 2  Write docs/look.md — palette as hex, typefaces and weights, typical shot length,
        how scenes hand off, camera behaviour, surface texture, how words arrive and leave.
Step 3  Write docs/shots.md for a [SECONDS]-second piece about [SUBJECT] in that grammar.
Step 4  Stop. Show me both. No code until I approve.
```
Describe the look and the limits; let the model choose the technique.

## 4 · Flow
One shape that never cuts away: it changes size, corner radius and colour from state to state, a cursor triggers every change, and the ending matches the beginning so it loops.
```
Ask me for: the product, the 8–12 screens that tell its story, real data for each,
brand colours and fonts, one accent, a track near [BPM] BPM, output formats.

Direction: product film, one container for the whole piece. Quiet neutral background.
Tiny overshoot at most. No glow, no particle bursts, no idle time.

Beat map ([BPM] BPM, 8 bars, something changes every beat):
  [state] → [state] → … → back to the first state.

Rules: one HTML stage driven by __paint(t); springs from engine/kit.js (chase() for any
value with several targets); words enter a beat after their container starts moving and
leave a beat before the next change; final frame equals first frame, cursor included.

First: ask for the inputs, then show me the states laid on the beat grid. Then code.
```

## 5 · Crew
```
You are director, animator, sound designer and render engineer for a [LENGTH] film. This is
a multi-session production — don't hurry to the final render.

THE FILM IN ONE SENTENCE   [what the viewer feels at the end]
INPUTS                     ./refs (take grammar, never content) · ./audio/track.wav (unaltered)
CAPABILITIES               skills: [list] · keys in .env: [list] · budget: [amount], spend sparingly
LOOK                       [palette, lettering, texture, camera]. Forbidden: [list]
BEATS                      0:00–0:02 the single strongest image · then a new payoff every 3–5 s ·
                           the last frame leads into the first

GATES (don't skip)
  1  look.md + shots.md (frames, camera, words, sounds). Show me; proceed after 10 minutes of silence.
  2  stills for every shot → contact sheet → review.
  3  rough cut at 540p with placeholder sound. Fix pacing now, not later.
  4  full animation → polish → sound → final render.
  5  one writer-agent per chapter, all following docs/STYLE-GUIDE.md, which you write first.

REVIEW (every shot, three rounds minimum) — use card 6; log in docs/review-log.md.
DELIVER   out/reel.mp4 · out/loop-check.mp4 · out/poster.png · out/contact.png · README.md
```
For clips a video model does better than hand-written code (physics, characters), let the model generate base footage, then redraw it in code so the final picture is entirely your own layer.

## 6 · Review
```
Open out/contact.png, out/strip.png and out/phone.png. Look at them properly and judge as a
tough director, not the author.

Score each from 1 to 10: opening hook · legibility at phone size · quality of motion ·
variety · composition · fidelity to the brand · sound sync.
Name the three worst problems with timestamps. Check for: words colliding mid-swap, things
sliding rather than settling, corner labels or borders, dead beats, soft scaled text, a
jump at the loop seam.
Fix them, re-render only the affected seconds, show new sheets and new scores. Stop at 8+.
```

## 7 · Retune
```
Replace every hand-written easing curve with kit.js springs. Pick a feel per element:
crisp for controls, calm for cards and camera, heavy for big type and logos, jelly for mascots.
Any value that gets retargeted uses chase(). Type never overshoots.
```

title: grid.mjs
synth.mjs
kit.js
forge.mjs
analyze.py
text:
"""Measure a supplied track and emit the same shape grid.mjs produces, plus accent points.

    python analyze.py track.wav > grid.json

Needs: pip install numpy librosa
Accents are moments of sudden energy (drum hits, stabs) where a visual should land.
"""
import json
import sys

import librosa
import numpy as np


def main(path: str) -> None:
    samples, rate = librosa.load(path, sr=22050, mono=True)
    envelope = librosa.onset.onset_strength(y=samples, sr=rate)

    tempo, beat_idx = librosa.beat.beat_track(onset_envelope=envelope, sr=rate)
    beats = librosa.frames_to_time(beat_idx, sr=rate)

    # Accents: envelope peaks that clear a rolling average by a margin.
    peak_idx = librosa.util.peak_pick(envelope, pre_max=4, post_max=4, pre_avg=6, post_avg=8, delta=0.4, wait=8)
    accents = librosa.frames_to_time(peak_idx, sr=rate)

    meter = 4
    json.dump({
        "bpm": round(float(np.atleast_1d(tempo)[0]), 2),
        "meter": meter,
        "offset": round(float(beats[0]), 4) if len(beats) else 0.0,
        "seconds": round(len(samples) / rate, 3),
        "beats": [round(float(b), 4) for b in beats],
        "bars": [round(float(b), 4) for b in beats[::meter]],
        "phrases": [round(float(b), 4) for b in beats[:: meter * 4]],
        "accents": [round(float(a), 4) for a in accents],
    }, sys.stdout, indent=1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    main(sys.argv[1])

title: reel.html
text:
<!doctype html>
<!-- Reel Forge stage — SHADDAI original.
     The page exposes one entry point for the renderer: window.__paint(t, blurSpan, taps).
     A reel is a list of "shots"; each shot paints itself from local time only. -->
<meta charset="utf-8">
<style>html,body{margin:0;background:#0b0d10}canvas{display:block}</style>
<canvas id="stage"></canvas>
<script type="module">
import { chase, spring, FEEL, remap, clamp01, seeded, cycle } from './kit.js';

const REEL = { width: 1080, height: 1920, seconds: 12, loop: true };
const ink = '#f4efe6', paper = '#0b0d10', accent = '#e8c45c';

const stage = document.getElementById('stage');
stage.width = REEL.width; stage.height = REEL.height;
const ctx = stage.getContext('2d');

// An off-screen buffer lets the renderer average several sub-moments into one
// frame (motion blur) without leaving the browser.
const acc = document.createElement('canvas'); acc.width = REEL.width; acc.height = REEL.height;
const actx = acc.getContext('2d');

// ── Shots ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Replace these with your own. Each paints using local time `t` (0 at its start).
const shots = [
  { at: 0, len: 4, paint(c, t) {
      const rise = spring(t - 0.05, ...FEEL.heavy);
      c.save(); c.translate(REEL.width / 2, REEL.height * 0.5 + (1 - rise) * 140);
      c.globalAlpha = remap(t, 0, 0.25);
      c.fillStyle = ink; c.font = '800 220px system-ui, sans-serif'; c.textAlign = 'center';
      c.fillText('FORGE', 0, 0);
      c.fillStyle = accent; c.fillRect(-300 * rise, 46, 600 * rise, 14);
      c.restore();
  }},
  { at: 4, len: 4, paint(c, t) {
      const dice = seeded(11);
      for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
        const col = i % 5, row = (i / 5) | 0;
        const pop = spring(t - row * 0.06 - dice() * 0.12, ...FEEL.crisp);
        const s = 150 * pop;
        c.fillStyle = (i * 7) % 11 === 0 ? accent : ink;
        c.fillRect(140 + col * 190 - s / 2, 380 + row * 190 - s / 2, s, s);
      }
  }},
];

// ── Paint ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function paintAt(c, t) {
  c.fillStyle = paper; c.fillRect(0, 0, REEL.width, REEL.height);
  const now = REEL.loop ? cycle(t, REEL.seconds) : t;
  for (const s of shots) if (now >= s.at && now < s.at + s.len) s.paint(c, now - s.at);
}

// span: seconds of shutter to blur across; taps: how many sub-moments to average.
window.__paint = (t, span = 0, taps = 1) => {
  if (taps <= 1 || span <= 0) { paintAt(ctx, t); return REEL; }
  actx.clearRect(0, 0, REEL.width, REEL.height);
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < taps; i++) {
    paintAt(actx, t - span * (1 - i / (taps - 1 || 1)));
    ctx.globalAlpha = 1 / (i + 1);                    // running average
    ctx.drawImage(acc, 0, 0);
  }
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
  return REEL;
};
window.__reel = REEL;

// Preview in a normal browser tab (the renderer drives frames itself).
if (!navigator.webdriver) {
  const t0 = performance.now();
  (function tick() { paintAt(ctx, (performance.now() - t0) / 1000); requestAnimationFrame(tick); })();
}
</script>
